_about: THE GLOSSARY, written once (the component plan's C3 and C9, approved 9 October 2026): the record's shorthand, each term with its name in full and what it means. components.py reads this file and the build writes it into site/components.js, between the WORDBOOK markers, as WORDBOOK.glossary. A key starting with '_' is a note and goes to neither.

WHAT DRAWS THESE (23 October 2026; until then this note said nothing did yet). The term popovers, since the component plan's step 6: a writer in either language marks a term <span data-term="ITL"> (components.term_mark, termMark in components.js), choosing the key by context -- RC is a roll call on a vote and the Regular Calendar in a committee's report, so the second is keyed RC-calendar -- and components.js makes the first on the page a button that opens its entry, on a tap, a hover held about half a second or keyboard focus, staying while the pointer moves onto it and closing on Escape (WCAG 1.4.13; the person, 9 October 2026). The vote words mark their abbreviations so (voteHead, and a recommendation's code on a committee's and a session day's pages). The glossary page lists every entry (below), and Learn's Using This Site draws its table 'Reading the shorthand' from these entries (civics._shorthand, 23 October 2026), so none of the three can define a term differently. FN, A and LOCAL are the suffixes on a bill's number.

THE WORDS ARE THE SITE'S OWN, as already published, and 'from' says where: Learn's 'Using this site' (its table 'Reading the shorthand', drawn from here since 23 October 2026, where the glossary's words replaced the table's for VV, DV, A, OT3rdg, Retain and OTPA), 'How a bill becomes law' (its table under 'How committees work'), the vote words the person approved on 8 October 2026 (only OTP, OTPA, ITL and IS are spelled as abbreviations on a vote), and the General Court's own docket key (records/docket_abbrev.json). 'says' is empty where the source gives the name alone.

THE GLOSSARY PAGE (14 October 2026): /learn/glossary lists every entry, A to Z by its name in full with the abbreviation after it, built by build_civics.py from this file, so the page and the popovers cannot disagree. Entries whose 'from' begins 'new, 14 October 2026' are new wording waiting for the person's check; the rest repeat what a Learn page already publishes.

OTP.name: Ought to Pass
OTP.says: a motion to pass the bill

OTPA.name: Ought to Pass with Amendment
OTPA.says: a motion to pass the bill with the committee's amendment
OTPA.from: using-this-site; says: new, 14 October 2026: the person to check

ITL.name: Inexpedient to Legislate
ITL.says: a motion to kill the bill

IS.name: Interim Study
IS.says: a motion to have the committee study the subject after the session; the bill itself goes no further this term

Retain.name: Retain
Retain.says: a House committee keeps the bill through the fall of the first year and reports it in the second

MA.name: Motion Adopted
MA.from: using-this-site; says: new, 14 October 2026: the person to check

MF.name: Motion Failed
MF.from: using-this-site; says: new, 14 October 2026: the person to check

VV.name: Voice vote
VV.says: a vote by the sound of the members' voices, with no count and no names recorded

DV.name: Division vote
DV.says: a vote that is counted, with the totals recorded but not who voted which way

RC-calendar.name: Regular Calendar
RC-calendar.says: the bills a chamber takes up one at a time, open to debate, rather than together on the consent calendar
RC-calendar.from: docket key; says: new, 14 October 2026: the person to check

CC.name: Consent Calendar
CC.says: the committee's recommendation, to pass, to kill or to send to interim study, adopted with the whole calendar in one vote, without floor debate

OT3rdg.name: Ordered to a third reading
OT3rdg.says: passed to the last stage before the chamber's final vote on the bill
OT3rdg.from: using-this-site; says: new, 14 October 2026: the person to check

HJ.name: House Journal
HJ.says: the chamber's own record of the day, cited by issue and sometimes page

SJ.name: Senate Journal
SJ.says: the chamber's own record of the day, cited by issue and sometimes page

FN.name: Fiscal note
FN.says: an estimate of what the bill would cost

A.name: Appropriation
A.says: the bill spends state money: it contains an appropriation, marked by an A after its number
A.from: using-this-site; says: new, 14 October 2026: the person to check

LOCAL.name: Local fiscal impact
LOCAL.says: the bill may change what towns, cities, counties or school districts spend or collect, marked LOCAL after its number
LOCAL.from: using-this-site; says: new, 14 October 2026: the person to check

LSR.name: Legislative Service Request
LSR.says: a legislator's request for a bill, filed with a title and an idea, mostly in the fall; attorneys at the Office of Legislative Services draft the text

HB.name: House Bill
HB.says: a proposed change to New Hampshire law; begins in the House, must pass both chambers, goes to the Governor

SB.name: Senate Bill
SB.says: begins in the Senate, otherwise the same as a House Bill

HR.name: House Resolution
HR.says: a formal, non-binding expression of opinion, policy preference, or internal rule; it does not go to the other chamber or the Governor and does not change any law

SR.name: Senate Resolution
SR.says: the Senate's own resolution: non-binding, and it does not go to the House or the Governor

HCR.name: House Concurrent Resolution
HCR.says: similar to a House Resolution, but voted on by both chambers

SCR.name: Senate Concurrent Resolution
SCR.says: similar to a Senate Resolution, but voted on by both chambers

CACR.name: Constitutional Amendment Concurrent Resolution
CACR.says: a proposed change to the state constitution, requiring a three-fifths vote in both chambers and a two-thirds majority of voters

Public hearing.name: Public hearing
Public hearing.says: the committee meeting where the sponsor introduces the bill and anyone may speak for or against it, or sign in without speaking; the committee takes no decision at it

Executive session.name: Executive session
Executive session.says: the committee meeting where it votes on what to recommend, usually days after the hearing; it cannot end the bill itself, because the recommendation goes to the floor

Work session.name: Work session
Work session.says: a committee or subcommittee meeting to work on a bill's text; open to the public, but the public is heard only at the public hearing
Work session.from: new, 14 October 2026: the person to check

Crossover.name: Crossover
Crossover.says: a bill moving from the chamber that passed it to the other one; there is a deadline for it each year

Committee of conference.name: Committee of conference
Committee of conference.says: where the chambers will not agree on a bill, members of both try to write a version each will accept; both chambers must then adopt the report unchanged

Concur.name: Concur
Concur.says: to agree to the other chamber's amendment; to nonconcur is to refuse it, after which a committee of conference may be asked for
Concur.from: new, 14 October 2026: the person to check

Enrolled.name: Enrolled bill
Enrolled.says: a bill both chambers have passed, given a final check of its text for errors before it is sent to the Governor

Veto.name: Veto
Veto.says: the Governor's refusal to sign a bill; it stands unless two thirds of each chamber override it

Override.name: Override
Override.says: two thirds of each chamber, by roll call, passing a bill over the Governor's veto; the House counts the two thirds among the members voting

Without signature.name: Law without signature
Without signature.says: a bill the Governor leaves unsigned for five days, Sundays excepted, becomes law without a signature, unless the legislature's adjournment prevents its return

Chaptered.name: Chaptered law
Chaptered.says: a bill that became law, numbered as a chapter of that year's session laws
Chaptered.from: new, 14 October 2026: the person to check

RSA.name: Revised Statutes Annotated
RSA.says: New Hampshire's laws in force, arranged by title and chapter; a bill changes the law by amending its sections
RSA.from: new, 14 October 2026: the person to check

Carried over.name: Carried over
Carried over.says: a bill retained in the first year that survives into the second and keeps its number

Laid on the table.name: Laid on the table
Laid on the table.says: set aside without a decision; it can be taken off the table later, and a bill still on the table when the term ends dies
Laid on the table.from: new, 14 October 2026: the person to check

Special order.name: Special order
Special order.says: a motion to take a bill up at a set time or place in the day's business, out of its turn on the calendar
Special order.from: new, 14 October 2026: the person to check

Reconsider.name: Reconsideration
Reconsider.says: a motion, made by a member who voted on the winning side, to take the same question again
Reconsider.from: new, 14 October 2026: the person to check

Rerefer.name: Re-referred
Rerefer.says: sent back to the committee it came from for more work
Rerefer.from: new, 14 October 2026: the person to check

Floor amendment.name: Floor amendment
Floor amendment.says: an amendment a member offers during floor debate, rather than one the committee recommends
Floor amendment.from: new, 14 October 2026: the person to check

Minority report.name: Minority report
Minority report.says: the written dissent of committee members who voted against the recommendation, printed beside the majority's report
Minority report.from: new, 14 October 2026: the person to check

Prime sponsor.name: Prime sponsor
Prime sponsor.says: the member who files the bill and introduces it at the hearing; members who join it are cosponsors
Prime sponsor.from: new, 14 October 2026: the person to check

Session day.name: Session day
Session day.says: a day the full House or Senate sits to vote on bills
Session day.from: new, 14 October 2026: the person to check

Died.name: Died
Died.says: ended without becoming law, however it ended: killed, left on the table, out of time when the session ended, lost between the chambers, or a veto that stood
Died.from: new, 17 October 2026: the person to check

Tabled.name: Tabled
Tabled.says: laid on the table while the session still sits; a bill still there when the session ends has died on the table
Tabled.from: new, 17 October 2026: the person to check

Indefinitely postponed.name: Indefinitely postponed
Indefinitely postponed.says: a vote that ends the bill for the term and, under the rules, bars the same subject from being taken up again before the term is out
Indefinitely postponed.from: new, 17 October 2026: the person to check

Floterial district.name: Floterial district
Floterial district.says: a House district laid over two or more neighboring districts, electing a representative of its own; its voters also elect their own district's
Floterial district.from: new, 17 October 2026: the person to check

Docket.name: Docket
Docket.says: the General Court's running list of every action taken on a bill, in the order it was recorded
Docket.from: new, 17 October 2026: the person to check

Organization Day.name: Organization Day
Organization Day.says: the first Wednesday of December after an election, when the new legislature is sworn in and elects its presiding officers
Organization Day.from: new, 14 October 2026: the person to check

Second committee.name: Second committee
Second committee.says: a bill that spends or raises money, sent on after the committee that heard it: in the House to Finance or to Ways and Means, in the Senate to Finance; such bills meet earlier deadlines in their first committee

Veto day.name: Veto day
Veto day.says: the day a chamber meets to take up the Governor's vetoes; overriding one takes two thirds of each chamber, by roll call
